question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 20% above the cost price. He sells one-fourth of the goods at the marked price and the remaining at 30% discount on the marked price. What is his gain/loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let the CP be ₹100

⇒ MP = ₹120 and SP at 30% loss = ₹84

By Mixture and Allegation method

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f39fbac9d85fac14023eedc220633c9f1d97d6a9bcf5b305ade0f687b5f16d7a.png] 

Overall SP = ₹93

⇒ Loss% = (100 - 93)/100 = 7%

∴ There will be a loss of 7%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Shopkeeper marks his goods 20% above the CP

1/4 of the goods are sold at MP

Remaining goods are sold at 30% discount

**Formula used:**

**1**. SP = MP × (100 - Discount%)/100

**2**. Loss% = [(CP - SP)/CP] × 100

**Calculation:**

Let CP of the goods be ₹100

⇒ MP = 100 × [(100 + 20)/100] = ₹120

According to the question,

Total SP = [(1/4) × 120] + [(3/4) × (70/100) × 120]

⇒ Total SP = 30 + 63 = ₹93

Loss% = [(100 - 93)/100] × 100

⇒ Loss% = (7/100) × 100 = 7%

∴ There will be a loss of 7%.
